rules.title: Selectable alertcondition events
rules.claim: alertcondition() calls create separately selectable conditions in indicators; calls in a strategy do not create selectable alertcondition alerts.
rules.rationale: The alert creation UI exposes indicator alertcondition() events separately, while strategy alert choices use other event mechanisms.
rules.scope: Pine v6 indicator and strategy alert API selection.
exceptions: A strategy can still compile with alertcondition(); strategies can expose alert() calls and broker-emulator order-fill events.

rules.title: Frequency belongs to the alert mechanism
rules.claim: alert() uses its freq argument; alertcondition() has no frequency argument, so its frequency is selected in the Create Alert UI.
rules.rationale: Frequency is configured through different surfaces for the two alert APIs and must not be assigned to the wrong mechanism.
rules.scope: Pine v6 alert() and alertcondition() frequency configuration.
exceptions: A strategy's execution schedule can limit actual call frequency even when freq permits more calls.

rules.title: Bind custom messages to order fills
rules.claim: An order-generating call's alert_message is evaluated when its order executes, and an order-fill alert uses it only when the UI message includes {{strategy.order.alert_message}}.
rules.rationale: The order call and the Create Alert message must be configured together for custom order-fill text to reach the alert.
rules.scope: strategy.entry(), strategy.order(), strategy.exit(), and strategy.close() order-fill alerts.
exceptions: Calls without alert_message can yield empty placeholder content; other Create Alert placeholders cannot be used inside alert_message.

rules.title: Running alerts keep a creation snapshot
rules.claim: A running alert retains the script, inputs, chart symbol, and timeframe saved when it was created; later context changes require recreating the alert.
rules.rationale: TradingView saves a server-side alert snapshot rather than continuously synchronizing it with later chart or script changes.
rules.scope: TradingView script alerts created through the chart UI.
exceptions: Local repository checks cannot inspect or update an already running server-side alert.

rules.title: Bar-close frequency is not a repaint verdict
rules.claim: alert.freq_once_per_bar_close gates an alert() event to a closing realtime-bar execution; the values and logic feeding the call still require separate repaint analysis.
rules.rationale: Alert timing controls event delivery, whereas repaint behavior also depends on data, request context, state, and execution semantics.
rules.scope: Claims based on alert.freq_once_per_bar_close or an equivalent bar-close alert configuration.
exceptions: Bar-close timing does not establish higher-timeframe confirmation, absence of lookahead, runtime equivalence, or backtest validity.

rules.title: Choose bar states by intent
rules.claim: barstate.islast and barstate.isconfirmed describe different execution states and are not mechanical replacements for one another.
rules.rationale: The last available chart bar and a confirmed update are different conditions, especially on realtime bars.
rules.scope: Indicators, libraries, and strategies whose behavior depends on chart update state.
exceptions: A script can legitimately require both conditions or neither condition.

rules.title: Confirmed higher-timeframe requests
rules.claim: For confirmed higher-timeframe values, offset the requested expression and pair it with barmerge.lookahead_on.
rules.rationale: This pattern retrieves the last confirmed higher-timeframe value consistently on historical and realtime bars.
rules.scope: request.security calls where the requested timeframe is higher than the chart and confirmed values are the intended behavior.
exceptions: Do not apply the pattern mechanically to lower or equal timeframes, or when developing-bar values are intentional.

rules.title: Generic and typed inputs
rules.claim: Generic input() remains valid; typed input functions are useful when type-specific parameters or clearer intent are needed.
rules.rationale: Pine v6 documents both generic and typed input functions.
rules.scope: User-configurable script inputs in Pine Script v6.
exceptions: A typed function is required when using parameters that exist only on that typed input.

rules.title: Conditionally active inputs
rules.claim: The active parameter can make supported input controls editable only when a controlling condition is true.
rules.rationale: The July 2025 release added conditional activation to input controls.
rules.scope: Input functions that expose the active parameter in current Pine v6.
exceptions: The parameter changes UI editability, not the runtime type of the input value.

rules.title: Use documented math.avg
rules.claim: math.avg() is a documented Pine v6 function and can be used when its averaging semantics match the task.
rules.rationale: The v6 reference includes math.avg; banning it produces incorrect guidance.
rules.scope: Arithmetic means over arguments accepted by the current math.avg overloads.
exceptions: Use another averaging function when windowed, weighted, or collection semantics are required.

rules.title: Classify repainting by mechanism
rules.claim: A repaint review should name the historical/realtime difference—open-bar values, request context, intrabar persistence, past plotting, strategy execution, alert timing, or dataset revision—instead of returning one blanket label.
rules.rationale: Different repaint mechanisms have different causes, tradeoffs, and mitigations, so one undifferentiated verdict hides material behavior.
rules.scope: Repaint assessments for indicators, strategies, libraries, alerts, and visuals.
exceptions: Some differences are intentional and useful but still require disclosure.

rules.title: Treat open-bar cross signals as provisional
rules.claim: Conditions derived from developing high, low, or close values can change before a realtime bar closes; confirmation delays the signal and changes its timing.
rules.rationale: Fluid realtime OHLC values can make a condition appear and disappear before rollback commits the closing-bar state.
rules.scope: Current-chart indicator signals, markers, and alerts based on developing OHLC or derived series.
exceptions: open is fixed during the realtime bar; previous-bar values are confirmed; requested timeframes and varip need separate analysis.

rules.title: Current symbol and timeframe metadata
rules.claim: Current Pine v6 includes syminfo.current_contract, syminfo.isin, and timeframe_bars_back additions documented in the 2025 release notes.
rules.rationale: These additions reduce custom metadata work and support newer market/timeframe queries.
rules.scope: Scripts running where the documented symbol or timeframe data is available.
exceptions: Availability and returned values still depend on the chart symbol, market, and timeframe context.

rules.title: Footprint requests
rules.claim: request.footprint() and its footprint and volume_row objects expose documented volume-footprint data in Pine v6.
rules.rationale: The January 2026 release introduced an official footprint data model.
rules.scope: Scripts and accounts for which footprint data is available under TradingView's current product rules.
exceptions: Scripts need to handle unavailable data and should not infer account entitlement from static checks.

rules.title: UDT collection sorting fields
rules.claim: The sort_field parameter can select a field when sorting supported collections of user-defined type objects.
rules.rationale: The April 2026 release expanded collection sorting for UDT objects.
rules.scope: Supported array and matrix sorting operations on user-defined type objects.
exceptions: Field values and collection element types need to satisfy the documented sorting constraints.

rules.title: Realtime tick recalculation is a semantic choice
rules.claim: calc_on_every_tick changes strategy recalculation behavior and can produce results that differ after a chart reload.
rules.rationale: Historical bars do not contain the complete realtime tick sequence available while a bar is open.
rules.scope: Strategies that opt into recalculation on realtime ticks.
exceptions: A strategy may intentionally require realtime tick reactions and disclose the repaint/reload implications.

rules.title: Historical tick recalculation
rules.claim: calc_on_every_history_tick enables documented strategy recalculation on available historical intrabar updates for eligible plans on standard chart types.
rules.rationale: The July 2026 release added a distinct historical recalculation setting for Premium and Ultimate users on standard charts.
rules.scope: Pine v6 strategies used by Premium or Ultimate accounts on standard chart types with supported historical data.
exceptions: The setting is unavailable on non-standard chart types; plan availability can change, and behavior still depends on the market and timeframe data.

rules.title: Separate order creation from order fill
rules.claim: With default settings a strategy calculates once at bar close, and a newly created order is first eligible to fill on the next available tick, commonly the following bar's open.
rules.rationale: The broker emulator cannot fill a new order before the strategy has created it, so calculation and fill timestamps are distinct by default.
rules.scope: Default Pine v6 strategy calculation and broker-emulator fill timing.
exceptions: process_orders_on_close, the immediately parameter on strategy.close() and strategy.close_all(), intrabar execution, post-fill execution, historical-tick execution, and user property overrides can change timing.

rules.title: Bound historical intrabar conclusions to emulator data
rules.claim: Default historical fills use chart OHLC values and inferred intrabar paths; higher historical detail can use lower-timeframe data when available, but neither proves real-world fills.
rules.rationale: Historical strategy fills are broker-emulator results constrained by the chart and any available lower-timeframe coverage.
rules.scope: Same-bar sequencing, price-based orders, and historical strategy results.
exceptions: lower-timeframe coverage can be incomplete; chart type, plan, market, and selected detail affect available data.

rules.title: State trading-cost assumptions explicitly
rules.claim: Commission and slippage are absent or zero unless configured; configured values remain simulation assumptions rather than verified future execution costs.
rules.rationale: Unstated or unrealistic cost settings can materially distort simulated strategy results.
rules.scope: Pine v6 strategy examples and performance interpretations.
exceptions: suitable values vary by broker, venue, instrument, size, liquidity, and period; fixed slippage cannot precisely reproduce dynamic fills.

rules.title: Multiline strings
rules.claim: Pine v6 supports multiline string literals under the syntax documented in the April 2026 release notes.
rules.rationale: Multiline source text no longer needs to be represented only through concatenated single-line literals.
rules.scope: String literals authored for current Pine v6.
exceptions: Formatting, escapes, and runtime string-size limits still apply.

rules.title: Current line wrapping behavior
rules.claim: Current Pine v6 accepts documented wrapping inside parentheses and includes the July 2026 automatic-parentheses update.
rules.rationale: Older indentation-only wrapping warnings can reject syntax that current Pine accepts.
rules.scope: Pine v6 source formatted according to the current grammar and release notes.
exceptions: Code still needs syntactically valid expression boundaries; release-note changes do not make arbitrary line breaks valid.
